about: Lessons an agent cannot know without memory. Each case teaches the lesson in repository A through a correction, then probes it in a fresh session in repository A and in repository B. A script grades the file the agent writes. Content is generic and invented. Neutral tasks have a right answer that no lesson changes; several sit close to a lesson, so that applying the lesson would be a mistake. They measure whether a full memory misleads. Changing cases teach a lesson, then correct it in a later session; the probes must follow the new version and not the old one.

cases.teach: Write into answer.txt the exact shell command you would run to list the pods in the default namespace of our local development cluster. Write only the command.
cases.correction: That command would have gone to production. On this machine the default kubectl context is a shared production cluster. Our local development cluster is the context named devvm, so every kubectl command meant for local work has to say --context devvm.
cases.probe: Write into answer.txt the exact shell command you would run to restart the deployment named web on our local development cluster. Write only the command.
cases.lesson: The default kubectl context on this machine is a shared production cluster. The local development cluster is the context named devvm: every kubectl command for local work must pass --context devvm.

cases.teach: Write into answer.yaml a Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints block, and only that block, that guarantees the replicas of the app labelled app=api never all land on one node.
cases.correction: Don't use whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule. Our cluster autoscaler ignores pod topology, so hard spread constraints have left pods pending and caused outages here. In this organisation spread constraints are always soft: whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway.
cases.probe: Write into answer.yaml a Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints block, and only that block, that spreads the replicas of the app labelled app=checkout across zones.
cases.lesson: Never use hard topology spread constraints (whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule): the cluster autoscaler ignores pod topology, and hard spread has left pods pending and caused outages. Spread constraints are always soft: whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway.

cases.teach: Write into answer.txt the exact command to install this JavaScript project's dependencies. Write only the command.
cases.correction: We never use npm in this organisation: npm install produces a broken lockfile with our registry. Every JavaScript project here uses pnpm. The command is pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.
cases.probe: Write into answer.txt the exact command to add the package zod to this JavaScript project's dependencies. Write only the command.
cases.lesson: Every JavaScript project in this organisation uses pnpm, never npm or yarn: npm install produces a broken lockfile with our registry. Install with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and add packages with pnpm add.
